items: All forms use Livewire 4 reactive components. When you change a field, the form reacts immediately on the server (no full page reload).

Cascading dropdowns (country->region->province->city->barangay, patient->philhealth member) use wire:model.live for real-time updates. Plain wire:model is deferred and would not re-render the dependent dropdown.
Never use wire:change - this throws DirectlyCallingLifecycleHooksNotAllowedException in Livewire 4. Use wire:model.live instead for cascading UI.
Pagination is standard across all list views. Use the page navigation controls at the bottom of lists.
Search boxes auto-filter on input (Livewire updatingX methods reset the page when the search term changes).
Modal dialogs are used for create/edit forms and detail views. Close modals with the X button or the Close button inside.
Flash messages (success/error) appear at the top of the page after actions. They auto-dismiss after a few seconds.
Table views show data in a grid with column headers. Click column headers to sort (ascending/descending toggle).
Print/PDF buttons generate documents server-side via DomPDF. The browser downloads the PDF file. Open it with your PDF viewer and print from there.
The sidebar/top navigation shows all accessible pages based on your permissions. Pages you cannot access are hidden.
The dashboard is the landing page after login. It shows today's activity and quick-access cards to major modules.

text: C. Data Flow: Patient Journey End to End
This section traces a typical patient's complete journey through the system, from registration to discharge, showing which modules and records are created at each step.

items: Patient arrives at hospital.

Step 1: Patient Registration - If new patient, register at Patients (/patients). Create patient record with demographics, address, contact, PhilHealth membership (if applicable). Patient code generated (e.g. 202600000001). If existing patient, skip to step 2.

Step 2: OPD Consultation Creation - At OPD, create OPD consultation (OPD > Consultations > Create New). Search/select patient. Fill: OPD Clinic, Attending Physician, Consultation Type, Visit Type, Referral Source. Save. Consultation code generated (OPD-00001). Status: Pending.
Step 3: Nursing Vitals Entry - Nurse enters vitals (BP, HR, temp, RR, weight, height, O2 sat, chief complaint) via Enter Vitals button. Status advances to In Progress.
Step 4: Doctor SOAP Documentation - Doctor fills SOAP: HPI, physical exam, assessment, treatment plan, orders summary, disposition, follow-up date. Status becomes Completed (if disposition set).
Step 5: Orders (if needed) - Doctor places orders: Lab (LR-XXXXX), Pharmacy (PR-XXXXX), CSR (CR-XXXXX), Radiology (Rad-XXXXX), Procedure (Proc-XXXXX). Each order created with request code and items.

Step 6: Order Fulfillment - Lab tech enters results (Lab > Results). Pharmacist dispenses (Pharmacy > Dispensing). CSR officer dispenses supplies (Supply > Dispensing). Rad tech performs exam, radiologist reports (Radiology > Results). Procedures performed (Procedures > Dispensing). Each updates the request status.

Step 7: Billing - Billing officer creates invoice (INV-XXXXX) from unbilled services (lab charges, pharmacy charges, CSR charges, radiology charges, procedure charges, manual charges). Applies discount if needed. Records patient payment (PAY-XXXXX). Prints invoice and receipt as needed.

Step 8: PhilHealth Claim (if eligible) - If patient has active PhilHealth membership and the visit qualifies, file PhilHealth claim (PhilHealth > Claims). Link to OPD consultation. Add services with RVS codes. Submit claim. Generate CF1-CF5 forms for submission.
Step 9: Certificate (if needed) - If patient needs a medical certificate, generate from Medical Records (/medical-records). Select certificate type, patient, encounter. Generate PDF.
Step 10: Follow-up - If follow-up needed, next_follow_up_date is set on the consultation. Patient returns for follow-up visit, new OPD consultation created.

text: C.2 Emergency Journey (ER admission to discharge)

items: Step 1: Triage - Patient arrives at ER. Create triage record (ER > Triage): patient, acuity level (1-5), mobility status, triage notes. Triage captures severity.
Step 2: ER Admission - Create ER admission (ER > Admission): patient, ER bed (status -> Occupied), attending physician, initial diagnosis, mode of arrival. Admission code: ER#<id>.

Step 3: Treatment - Doctor fills treatment form: HPI, physical exam, assessment, orders summary, treatment notes, OECB (if applicable - add OECB entries with core presentation, auto-fetches package code and fixed fee), disposition, discharge instructions.
Step 4: Orders - Doctor places orders from ER: Lab (LR-), Pharmacy (PR-), CSR (CR-), Radiology (Rad-), Procedure (Proc-). Priority defaults to 'Urgent' for ER.
Step 5: Order Fulfillment - Same as OPD (lab results, pharmacy dispensing, CSR dispensing, radiology exam+report, procedure performance).

Step 6: EECL PDF (if OECB) - If is_oecb=true, generate EECL PDF (route: er.admission.eeclpdf). PDF includes all OECB entries, triage, bed/zone, diagnosis, disposition. For emergency billing/PhilHealth.

Step 7: Disposition - Set final disposition: Discharged (goes home), Admitted (transferred to inpatient ward/ICU), Referred (to another facility), Left Without Being Seen, Against Medical Advice, Expired. Bed status updated (occupied bed -> Available if discharged).
Step 8: Billing - Billing officer creates invoice (INV-XXXXX) from ER charges. Records payment. If PhilHealth member, file PhilHealth claim (Emergency type). Generate EECL claim form PDF.

Step 9: Inpatient Admission (if admitted) - If disposition = Admitted, create inpatient admission (Admission /admission): patient, admitting diagnosis, attending physician, admission type, ward room or ICU bed (status -> Occupied). Admission code: ADM#<id>. The ER admission links to the inpatient admission.

Step 1: Inpatient Admission - Create admission (Admission /admission): patient, admitting diagnosis, attending physician, admission type, ward room or ICU bed (status -> Occupied), admission date. Admission code: ADM#<id>.

Step 2: Ward/ICU Care - Throughout stay: vitals, nursing notes, physician rounds, orders (lab, pharmacy, CSR, radiology, procedure daily), medications dispensed, procedures performed. All linked to the admission record. Bed/room status managed. MICU patients get periodic assessment parameters.

Step 3: OR Procedure (if needed) - Schedule OR procedure (OR > Schedule): patient, OR room, procedure type/description, surgeon, anesthesiologist, date/time. Perform procedure: intra-op notes, post-op notes. OR schedule updates.

Step 4: Discharge - On discharge: set discharge date, discharge diagnosis, discharge disposition, discharge instructions. Bed/room status freed (Occupied -> Available). Admission status becomes 'Discharged'.

Step 5: Billing - Billing officer creates invoice (INV-XXXXX) from all inpatient charges (cumulative lab, pharmacy, CSR, radiology, procedure charges, room/bed charges, OR charges, etc.). Records payment. If PhilHealth, file inpatient claim (Inpatient type). Generate CF1-CF5 forms.
Step 6: Certificate - If needed, generate discharge summary/medical certificate from Medical Records.
Step 7: Follow-up - If follow-up needed, patient returns to OPD. New OPD consultation created, linked to admission if needed.

All models use $timestamps = false - there are no automatic created_at/updated_at columns. Instead, audit columns created_by, created_date, updated_by, updated_date are managed explicitly in every create() and update() call.
All models use $guarded = ['id'] - all other fields are mass-assignable.

Soft deletes use a history column: 1 = current/active, 0 = deactivated. The global scope filters to history = 1. To query across all history states or across tenants, use withoutGlobalScopes() and re-add ->where('history', 1) and ->where('tenant_id', $tid) manually.

Tenant scoping: all tenant-scoped models use the ScopedByTenant trait. This trait automatically adds ->where('tenant_id', request()->attributes->get('tenant_id')) to every query. The tenant_id is set on the request when a user logs in.
Foreign keys follow Laravel conventions: {relation}_id (e.g. patient_id, department_id, health_care_professional_id).

Audit columns: created_by (int - user ID), created_date (datetime), updated_by (int - user ID), updated_date (datetime). Set explicitly on every create/update. For public booking (no authenticated user), created_by/updated_by can be null.
Multi-tenancy: tenant_id = hospitals.id. DEMO hospital = id 1. All tenant-scoped records have tenant_id field. When running raw queries or withoutGlobalScopes, always filter by tenant_id.
Unique constraints often include tenant_id and history in the rule (e.g. unique:patients,patient_code,NULL,id,tenant_id,{tid},history,1). This ensures uniqueness per tenant per active record.
MS SQL Server quirks: SUBSTRING takes 3 arguments (expression, start, length). Unlike MySQL, there is no 2-argument form. When writing raw SQL with DB::statement(), use SUBSTRING correctly.
Relationships: Eloquent relationships (belongsTo, hasMany, belongsToMany) are standard. Some models use belongsToThrough for indirect relationships (e.g. PayoutTransaction -> SC via PayoutCutoff).
Stack: Laravel 12, PHP 8.2.12, XAMPP on Windows, Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL) database. Frontend: Livewire 4, Tailwind CSS v4, Alpine.js v3.15, Vite 7.
Environment: .env file contains APP_URL, DB_CONNECTION=sqlsrv, DB_HOST=127.0.0.1, DB_PORT=1433, DB_DATABASE=sithemr, DB_USERNAME=root, DB_PASSWORD=P@ssw0rd.
Do NOT install doctrine/dbal - use raw DB::statement() for column changes (schema modifications). The project explicitly avoids doctrine/dbal.

Frontend build: npm run build - compiles Vite assets (CSS + JS) to public/build/. Run this after any Blade/Vue/Tailwind changes. npm run dev runs hot-reload dev server. package.json has "type": "module" - E2E test scripts must be .cjs files.

JWT Auth: tymon/jwt-auth v2.3. JWT token stored in HTTP-only cookie 'jwt_token'. JwtMiddleware wraps the entire web group. Public routes must be explicitly added to the skip list in app/Http/Middleware/JwtMiddleware.php.
Livewire 4: use wire:model.live for cascading UI. NEVER wire:change. snake_case for public component properties.
PDF Engine: Barryvdh DomPDF v3.1. All PDF generation is server-side. PDF templates are Blade templates rendered to HTML then converted to PDF. PDFs are downloaded by the browser.
Spreadsheet: PHPOffice PHPSpreadsheet v5.8. Used for Excel export in reports.

E2E Testing: Playwright installed locally only (not in package.json - run npm install playwright --no-save). Browser downloaded (npx playwright install chromium). Test scripts must be .cjs (because package.json has "type": "module"). Run with node. Delete after passing.
Admin login: admin@demohospital.com / Admin@12345 (DEMO hospital, tenant ID 1).
Public booking: /book-appointment is the only route accessible without login. Patients self-book appointments. The booking generates appointment_code (APT-XXXXX format).
Rate limiting: /login throttled to 10 attempts per 1 minute.
Multi-tenancy: tenant_id = hospitals.id. ScopedByTenant trait auto-filters. DEMO hospital = id 1.
History soft delete: history column (1=current). Global scope filters history=1. When using withoutGlobalScopes(), add ->where('history', 1) and ->where('tenant_id', $tid) manually.

Debugging tips: (1) If a dropdown is empty, check if master data exists for your tenant. (2) If you get 403, check your role's permissions. (3) If a page expired, refresh and log in again. (4) For raw SQL on MSSQL, remember SUBSTRING needs 3 args. (5) For queries across tenants, use withoutGlobalScopes() + manual tenant/history filters.
